_comment: Runtime config for the DoseRAD2026 algorithm container. Lives in the model tarball
so parameters can be changed by re-uploading ~12 MB instead of rebuilding the ~15 GB
image. Precedence: built-in default < this file < environment variable.
Unknown keys are logged and ignored. Effective values are printed at startup as
'[config] effective: {...}'.
GPU peak, REFITTED after the BEV-crop fix (2026-07-26):
peak GiB ~= 1.74 + 1.73 * dense_hook_batch_items   (at 30 beamlets/chunk)
The old model (0.8 + 5.04 * items + 0.089 * beamlets) was measured while the
container ran the correction net on a 44x128 BEV instead of the trained 26x74 --
2.93x the voxels. Per-item cost fell 5.04 -> 1.73 GiB, exactly that ratio, so the
old '<= 2 on an A10G' limit was the bug, not a capability limit.
Measured on the fixed path: items=2 -> 5.20 allocated / 7.31 reserved;
items=6 -> 12.11 allocated / 18.45 reserved.
Size against RESERVED (~1.5x allocated). items=4 predicts ~8.7 allocated /
~13 GiB reserved, leaving ~9 GiB margin on a 24 GB A10G. items=6 leaves only
~3.9 GiB and is not worth the risk on a scored run. On OOM the container shrinks
the dense batch itself, then splits the ray group, so a run recovers rather than fails.
MR-to-sCT benchmark on registered case 1ABB011 (22,939,290 voxels):
FP32: 8.643 s, 2.352 GiB peak reserved, body CT MAE 24.749716 HU
FP16: 3.814 s, 1.514 GiB peak reserved, body CT MAE 24.750071 HU
FP16 is 2.266x faster; its sCT-vs-FP32 RMSE is 0.202589 HU and changes body
CT MAE by only +0.000355 HU. Output is clipped to the bundle's recorded training
range [-1024, 3071] before proton density/material conversion.
